papers.claim: Using White's Reality Check bootstrap over ~7,846 rules on 100 years of DJIA data, the best Brock-era rule survives data-snooping adjustment IN-sample but does NOT deliver superior performance in the subsequent OUT-of-sample decade -- once you correct for rule-mining, technical-trading profitability is far weaker.
papers.approach: White's Reality Check over a ~7,846-rule universe (filters, MAs, breakouts, channels, OBV) to test whether the best mined rule survives data-snooping and holds out of sample.

assumptions.notes: The data-snooping NEGATIVE control: mine enough rules and one looks great in-sample but decays OOS. Directly relevant to sweeping many technical_* configs -- the caution, not a strategy to run.

papers.verdictNote: The essential CAUTION for BlackSwan's technical sweeps: the more (indicator x threshold x direction) rules we grid, the more a 'winner' is data-snooping, not edge. Mirrors our OOS-across-windows + seed-stability bar -- a technical config counts only if it holds across 2022/23/24, never just the best single-window cell. This paper's replicateConfig IS a wide rule grid, on purpose.

models.name: Recurrent PPO (custom LSTM)
models.description: On-policy PPO with an LSTM that carries state across bars plus a regularised custom actor-critic head. The default/winner and the closest practical realisation of direct/recurrent RL on a risk-adjusted utility.

models.name: Recurrent PPO (GRU core)
models.description: On-policy RecurrentPPO whose recurrent core is a GRU carried across bars in the POLICY (not a features-extractor) — the lighter-gate sibling of the reppo LSTM arm. 'gru-custom' adds the regularised custom actor-critic head. Expected ~wash vs LSTM.

models.name: Recurrent PPO (S4D diagonal SSM core)
models.description: On-policy RecurrentPPO whose recurrent core is a diagonal state-space model (S4D) threaded across env steps in the POLICY — an SSM FALSIFICATION arm vs the LSTM/GRU cores. The complex SSM state is packed real/imag into the SB3 (hidden, cell) slots; ssm_state_dim sets the modes per channel. 's4d-custom' adds the custom head.

models.name: PPO
models.description: Proximal Policy Optimization (clipped surrogate, on-policy). Covers the stock SB3 MLP policy, the custom regularised actor-critic head (ppo-custom), and the JAX/SBX build.

models.name: TRPO
models.description: Trust-region (KL-constrained) policy gradient; covers the custom-head and stock-MLP variants.

models.name: Attention-PPO
models.description: PPO over a true sequence features-extractor: single-block self-attention with a learned positional embedding over the reshaped bar grid (vs reppo's LSTM).

models.name: DQN
models.description: Deep Q-network (replay buffer + target net). Covers the stock MLP policy, the custom head, the LSTM features-extractor variant, the JAX/SBX build, and Théate & Ernst's Trading DQN (TDQN) — mechanically the custom-head DQN under a specific launch config.

models.name: Dueling DQN
models.description: Off-policy Q-learning with separate value + advantage streams. Consolidates every dueling variant: custom head, the LSTM features-extractor flavours (hidden 2/3/4), and the stock dueling policy.

models.name: Munchausen DQN
models.description: DQN augmented with the Munchausen term (a scaled log-policy bonus added to the reward) — implicit KL-regularised policy iteration. Consolidates the plain, custom-head, and dueling+LSTM Munchausen variants.

models.name: Rainbow DQN
models.description: DQN with prioritized experience replay, NoisyNet exploration, dueling streams and distributional quantiles. Consolidates the custom head and the SB3-subclass build.

models.name: Implicit Quantile Network (IQN)
models.description: Distributional RL that samples implicit quantiles of the return distribution (quantile-Huber loss); covers the stock and custom-quantile-network variants. Implemented in code, not in the active sweep set.

models.name: Agent57
models.description: DQN with an Agent57-style intrinsic-reward exploration buffer (count-based + prediction-error + episodic-memory novelty). Fixed 2026-06-26: CustomAgent57ReplayBuffer now records the sampled buffer positions (last_sampled_indices) so compute_intrinsic_rewards can look the per-sample bonus up — SB3's ReplayBufferSamples carries no indices.

models.name: Ensemble (4x Dueling DQN)
models.description: A bagged ensemble of four custom dueling-DQN agents. Trains each member independently and predicts by AVERAGING their Q-values then argmax (the discrete-action ensemble vote). Fixed 2026-06-26: reimplemented as a plain duck-typed model (learn/predict/save/policy/device) instead of an unfinished OffPolicyAlgorithm subclass.

models.name: Supervised (logistic regression)
models.description: Non-RL control: a logistic-regression classifier predicts next-bar direction from the same features and a fixed rule trades on it through the unchanged environment.

models.name: Supervised (gradient-boosted trees)
models.description: Non-RL control: a gradient-boosted-tree classifier (the decisive 'is RL even the right tool?' baseline) forecasting next-bar direction.

models.name: Buy-and-Hold
models.description: Passive control - buys at the first bar and holds to the end; the benchmark every active model must beat out-of-sample net of fees.

models.name: iTransformer sequence encoder (PPO)
models.description: PPO over an inverted-attention (iTransformer, Liu et al. 2024) sequence encoder — each VARIATE (feature column) is a token embedding its full lookback series, with attention ACROSS variates (no positional embedding; variates are unordered). A third SequenceFeaturesExtractor variant to A/B against attn-ppo (attention over time) and tcn-ppo. Built 2026-06-26 (sequence_extractor.py `encoder='itransformer'`).

models.name: A2C
models.description: Advantage Actor-Critic — a synchronous on-policy actor-critic. Covers the stock SB3 MLP build and the tuned custom-net-arch head. Also the project's Policy-Gradient representative (Zhang/Zohren/Roberts 2020): vanilla REINFORCE is subsumed by A2C, which adds a learned baseline and is strictly stronger.

models.name: QR-DQN
models.description: Quantile-Regression DQN — distributional RL that learns a set of return quantiles (via quantile-Huber regression) instead of a single Q-value. Covers the SB3-contrib build and the custom quantile net.

models.name: ARS
models.description: Augmented Random Search — a gradient-free baseline that perturbs policy weights along random directions and keeps the best. A decisive control: if random search rivals the gradient learners, the learned gradient isn't earning its keep.

models.name: Time-Series Momentum
models.description: A non-RL time-series-momentum baseline (Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen 2012): take a long/short position on the sign of the trailing return over a lookback. The rule-based trend-following control — 'does a learned policy actually beat simple momentum net of fees?'.

models.name: Recurrent Reinforcement Learning (RRL)
models.description: Moody & Saffell (2001) DIRECT recurrent RL — no Q-values, no SB3. A recurrent linear policy F_t = tanh(w·x_t + u·F_{t-1} + b) outputs a CONTINUOUS position in [-1,1] (the previous position feeds back, so it holds through noise), trained by gradient ASCENT on the Sharpe ratio of the realised strategy return R_t = F_{t-1}·r_t − δ·|ΔF| (the objective the online DIFFERENTIAL Sharpe estimates), via truncated BPTT. Single-asset; the continuous position is discretised to the env's discrete long/flat/short actions at eval.

models.name: ESN-RRL (Echo State Network + RRL)
models.description: Borrageiro (2022) — RRL on top of a fixed ECHO STATE NETWORK reservoir. A random recurrent net, scaled to a sub-unit spectral radius (the echo-state property), is run over the inputs WITHOUT training; its high-dimensional leaky-integrator state is the feature the trained RRL position layer reads (only the readout learns). Inherits RRL's direct Sharpe-ascent training + discretised-action eval; only the feature map differs.

models.name: EIIE (Ensemble of Identical Independent Evaluators)
models.description: DEFERRED — a multi-asset PORTFOLIO architecture (Jiang et al 2017): one weight-shared network is applied INDEPENDENTLY to each asset's price tensor, producing a softmax allocation over N assets + cash. It cannot be built faithfully in BlackSwan's SINGLE-asset, discrete-action env (it degenerates to a position sizer). Revisit once the multi-asset / portfolio env lands (Wave-3).
models.proposal: Needs a multi-asset portfolio env first (continuous weight-vector action over N assets + cash); then the EIIE extractor (weight-shared per-asset CNN/RNN -> softmax weights). Blocked until that env exists.

models.name: Time-of-Day Baseline
models.description: A deterministic clock strategy: open a long at a fixed UTC hour and close at another, every day — an intraday round-trip (buy<sell) or an OVERNIGHT hold (buy>sell). A control to BEAT and a probe for time-of-day / overnight seasonality; needs intraday data (timeframe=1h). Sweep time_buy x time_sell to surface any hour-of-day pattern. Per the literature (intraday momentum is an equity open/close-auction effect; crypto calendar effects are regime-dependent and cost-fragile) these rarely survive 0.1% fees on a 24/7 asset — so the value is the baseline + the falsification.

models.name: Day-of-Week Baseline
models.description: A deterministic weekly clock: open a long at the start of weekday `day_buy` (0=Mon..6=Sun) and close at `day_sell`, every week — an intra-week hold (buy<sell, e.g. Mon->Fri) or a WEEKEND hold (buy>sell, e.g. Fri->Mon; crypto trades the weekend). A control to BEAT and a probe for weekly seasonality (the Monday / day-of-week effect; Aharon-Qadan). Runs at a daily step (timeframe=1d). Per the literature these calendar effects are in-sample, data-mining-prone and unlikely to survive OOS net of 0.1% fees — so the value is the baseline + falsification.

models.name: Sequence Features Extractor
models.description: An SB3 features extractor that encodes the lookback window with a modern sequence model — single-block self-attention, a dilated-causal TCN, or an inverted-transformer (iTransformer) — instead of flattening the bars. The shared sequence backbone behind the attn-ppo / tcn-ppo / itransformer-ppo models.

models.name: LSTM Features Extractor (LSTMFCE)
models.description: A recurrent (LSTM) features extractor that carries hidden state across bars before the value/policy head — the sequence memory reused by the DQN-family `*-lstm` variants.

models.name: Custom MLP Extractor
models.description: A configurable shared-trunk MLP feature extractor for actor-critic policies, letting trunk width/depth follow the `net_arch` lever.

models.name: Custom Policies & Q-Nets
models.description: The custom policy library the `*-custom` models train through: regularised ActorCritic and RecurrentActorCritic heads plus DQN, Dueling, Rainbow and QR-DQN policies.

models.name: Custom IQN Policy
models.description: An Implicit Quantile Network policy and its quantile network (CustomIQNPolicy / CustomQuantileNetwork) for distributional value estimation, used by the iqn-custom model.

models.name: Custom Q-Network
models.description: A configurable Q-network builder (`create_mlp_custom`) that tiles a `-custom` recipe's hidden block pattern to an exact layer count — the shared Q-head for the custom DQN family.

models.name: Dueling DQN Policy
models.description: A dueling Q-head that splits estimation into separate value and advantage streams (DuelingQNetwork / DuelingDQNPolicy), reducing action-value variance.

models.name: Prioritized Replay Buffer
models.description: A proportional prioritized experience-replay buffer that samples transitions by TD-error priority — the replay component behind the Rainbow / prioritized-DQN line.

models.name: Agent57 Replay Buffer & Episodic Memory
models.description: Agent57's replay buffer paired with an episodic-memory module (CustomAgent57ReplayBuffer / EpisodicMemory) that supplies an intrinsic novelty signal.

models.name: DGWO — Grey-Wolf Optimizer
models.description: A Grey-Wolf-guided gradient optimizer (gradient-descent update plus a decaying metaheuristic exploration pull toward a tracked leader), selectable via the `optimizer_class` lever as an experimental alternative to Adam/RMSprop.

models.name: Attention Blocks
models.description: A kit of attention modules — scaled-dot-product, multi-head, additive, global-context and a self-attention wrapper — selectable as blocks in the custom Q-network `custom_net_arch` recipes (consumed by `create_mlp_custom`).

models.name: NN Building Blocks
models.description: Small reusable NN primitives for assembling custom policies: NoisyLinear (NoisyNet exploration, `noisylinear.py`), DropConnectLinear (`dropconnect.py`), ResidualBlock (`residualblock.py`), DenseBlock (`denseblock.py`), and local LSTM/GRU memory cells (`memorymodels.py`).
